🚁 Epic drone flyover of Tesla's Fremont Factory!

Captured some incredible and historic footage today:  Cybercabs actively testing — smoothly handling speed bumps before launching hard down the track. I also spotted Model S and Model X vehicles in the launch area along with what appear to be some of the final S & X rolling off the assembly line as their legendary run at Fremont wraps up.

The Model Y production line was surprisingly quiet during the flight, but I got great aerial views of the busy shipping yard and the factory’s recycling area too.

From next-gen Cybercab action to the end of an era with the S & X — this flyover really shows the transition happening at one of the world’s most important EV factories. Fremont never disappoints!

What do you think about the Cybercab testing and the final S/X coming off the line? Drop your thoughts in the comments 👇

TESLA AI5 CHIP: THE NEXT GIANT LEAP IN AUTONOMY & ROBOTICS

Tesla has officially taped out the AI5 chip — the next-generation inference processor that will power the future of Full Self-Driving, Optimus, and massive supercomputer clusters.

This is a huge milestone.

Key details on AI5:
•Massive performance jump over AI4 (Musk has described it as up to 40x better in certain metrics, with a single AI5 delivering roughly 5x the useful compute of two AI4 chips).
•Optimized for Tesla’s end-to-end neural nets — designed specifically for real-time inference in vehicles and robots.
•Will first go into Optimus robots and Tesla’s supercomputer clusters before potentially appearing in vehicles.
•Manufacturing will be handled by TSMC and Samsung, with volume production targeted for 2027.
•AI6 and Dojo 3 are already in the works, showing Tesla’s aggressive chip roadmap.

This chip is existential for Tesla’s long-term vision. It will enable much larger, more capable neural networks for FSD, dramatically improve robot performance, and help Tesla build some of the most powerful AI training clusters on the planet.
The vertical integration advantage is real: Tesla designs both the hardware and the software stack, giving it an edge that’s hard for competitors to match.

The AI5 is another reminder that Tesla is not just a car company — it’s becoming one of the most advanced AI hardware companies in the world.
